_note: Scaled synthetic benchmark. The paper reports its results only as curves (risk vs. epsilon, accuracy vs. tokens) on real LLM trajectories, so it has no scalar values on this benchmark's scale; its findings are recorded verbatim under each experiment's '_paper_reported'. 'results' holds this gym's reference numbers on the held-out test (scripts/evaluate_test.sh), not paper numbers. Ranking: token_savings and accuracy are scored; risk metrics are constraints enforced by the evaluator's gate (a run whose realized risk exceeds the target at more than 15% of operating points is scored as failed), so they carry coefficient 0.

adaptive_budget_efficiency.description: Natural solvable mix (about 58% of instances solvable within budget); 400 labelled calibration examples per draw, 4 draws per profile, target risks 0.10/0.15/0.20. Adaptive stopping should save reasoning tokens while realized risks stay within the target.
adaptive_budget_efficiency.notes: Scaled synthetic benchmark: simulated reasoning trajectories from held-out (model, dataset) profiles; values in 'results' are this gym's reference runs, not paper numbers.
adaptive_budget_efficiency._paper_reported: Paper (Sec. 5.3, Fig. 5-6): at a fixed risk tolerance, risk-controlled adaptive stopping reaches comparable accuracy with fewer total tokens; adding the lower threshold shifts the accuracy-vs-tokens curve left. Reported only as curves (Qwen3-8B/30B, R1-Distill-32B, Qwen3-VL-8B on AIME, DeepScaleR, GPQA, MathVision); no scalar values.

accuracy.description: Fraction of held-out questions answered correctly at the stopping point (a defer/abstain counts as incorrect), averaged over calibration draws, profiles and target risk levels.

token_savings.description: One minus the fraction of full-budget reasoning tokens consumed, with tokens charged up to the chunk where the policy stopped; averaged over operating points.

solvable_accuracy.description: Diagnostic: accuracy on instances whose full-budget answer is correct.

unsolvable_token_savings.description: Diagnostic: token savings on instances whose full-budget answer is wrong.

false_positive_risk.description: Constraint (gated, unscored): fraction of instances where the policy stopped before the budget and emitted a wrong answer.

false_negative_risk.description: Constraint (gated, unscored): premature-defer loss, i.e. for deferred instances the fraction of remaining chunks whose answer would have been correct, averaged over all instances.

violation_rate.description: Constraint (gated, unscored): fraction of operating points where realized false-positive or false-negative risk exceeds the target epsilon. Above 0.15 the experiment is scored as failed.

constraint_satisfied.description: Diagnostic: 1 if the violation rate is within the allowed 0.15, else 0 (failed runs receive the failure values for every metric).

defer_precision.description: Diagnostic: fraction of defers on instances whose full-budget answer is wrong.

budget_exit_fraction.description: Diagnostic: fraction of instances that consumed the whole budget.

risk_control.description: Small-calibration regime: 50 labelled calibration examples per draw, 10 draws per profile, target risks 0.05/0.10/0.20/0.25, on held-out profiles disjoint from the other experiments. Realized risk must stay within the target across calibration draws (gate), and the policy should still save tokens.
risk_control.notes: Scaled synthetic benchmark: simulated reasoning trajectories from held-out (model, dataset) profiles; values in 'results' are this gym's reference runs, not paper numbers.
risk_control._paper_reported: Paper (Sec. 5.2, Fig. 4, Fig. 7): over 40 random validation/test splits with 50 validation examples, UCB-calibrated thresholds keep realized test risk below epsilon, while naive validation tuning frequently exceeds it; the gap widens for smaller validation sets (8/16/40). Reported only as curves.
